aliases: Camellia sinensis var. pubilimba cv. Danxia 1
processing: A 2023 draft group standard lists this cultivar as raw material for white tea, with top grades made from single buds or one bud and one leaf. Other processing is little documented.
harvest_season: Not well documented for this cultivar; as with other northern Guangdong teas, spring is the usual main picking.
appearance_dry: Likely downy, as is typical of the hairy-leaved variety it belongs to; no detailed description is on record.
appearance_liquor: No reliable description exists; expect a pale yellow-green if it is made as a green tea.
taste_profile: No reliable tasting record exists for this cultivar on its own, so any cup notes depend on the maker; a clean green tea character is what its class suggests.

brewing.notes: General green tea advice, because no brewing tradition specific to this cultivar is recorded. Adjust if the tea is made in another style.

vintage_note: There is no documented market for this cultivar under its own name. Where it reaches the cup as green tea, the usual rule applies: the current spring harvest, drunk within about a year.
description:
Danxia 1 is a clonal tea cultivar of Camellia sinensis var. pubilimba, the hairy-leaved tea variety. A 2023 draft group standard for white-haired white tea names it among the Danxia clones selected from the white-haired tea populations of the Shaoguan area in northern Guangdong, but little else is published about the plant.

The local context helps. Renhua is known for its white-haired tea, a protected regional product, and the county promotes a 'Danxia white tea' brand. The draft standard allows this cultivar as raw material for white tea, including top grades of single buds or one bud and one leaf.

As a drinker, you are unlikely to see it on a label, since no market under its own name is documented.

If a seller does offer it, ask how it was processed and where it was grown. That will tell you much more than the cultivar name alone.
history: Little is documented. The cultivar is recorded under its botanical name, but its breeder, its release date and its selection history are not publicly clear.
